To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) it is theoretically impossible for any classifier to be robust to adversarial examples; and (2) generative models are not robust to adversarial attacks.

(1) it is impossible to detect worst case outliers with likelihood based generativem models, (2) it is possible to detect ambiguous inputs with likelihood based generativediscriminative models, (3) the maximum likelihood training criterion leads to a variety of undesirable model behaviors that make likelihood based generative classifiers ineffective for robust classification and (4) we can overcome the limitations of likelihood based generative classifier by introducing a new training objective.

(1) Robustness against adversarial examples can not be guaranteed for any generative classification model; (2) Robustness can be achieved on MNIST, but not on CIFAR10; (3) Robustness breaks down on CIFER10 because generative models trained with the likelihood objective have undesirable properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: Can likelihood based generative classifiers deliver on their promises? What is the theoretical limit of robustness of generative classifiers? How can we improve robustness of likelihood based generative classification models?

the following questions: (i) Can we theoretically characterize the robustness of conditional generative models? (ii) How can we practically train robust generative models? and (iii) What are their limitations?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
likelihood based generative classifiers are not suitable for robust classification.
likelihood based generative classifiers can not be robust.
generative models are not suitable for robust classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
while we are not able to guarantee the robustness of generative classifiers, we can identify some of the reasons that make them ineffective.
we show that it is not possible to achieve adversarial robustness for generative models.
while likelihood based generative classifiers are not effective for robust classification, they can still be useful for other applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
robust classification is an ill posed problem that can only be solved in a meaningful way by explicitly modeling the distribution of outliers.
the robustness properties of generative classifiers are highly dependent on the choice of model architecture and training objective.

while likelihood based generative classifiers may seem to be the natural choice for robust classification, in practice they are not robust to even small adversarial perturbations and are prone to overfitting to the training data.
